mainTopic: The order of a תענית ציבור, and whether bathing in cold water is allowed on fasts and for an אבל: רב חסדא's split between mourning and pleasure, the challenges to it, and רבא's lenient view.
overview: The amud opens by finishing a discussion about the order of a תענית ציבור. Using פסוקים from עזרא, the גמרא shows that dealing with the community's sins comes first and prayer comes after. Then רב חסדא teaches that when bathing is banned because of mourning (תשעה באב, an אבל), even cold water is forbidden. When it is banned only to remove pleasure (a תענית ציבור), only hot water is forbidden. A proof for the fast-day leniency comes from the משנה's extra phrase 'they lock the bathhouses.' The גמרא then tries to prove the mourning rule from a ברייתא about חייבי טבילות, but that proof is pushed off. Next, a ברייתא linking fast-day bans to an אבל challenges the fast-day leniency, and the גמרא answers it. A story about רבי יוסי בן רבי חנינא bathing in cold water during שבעה challenges the mourning rule; it is answered as a special case of mournings that came one after another. Finally, רבא rules that an אבל may bathe in cold water, and a challenge to him is announced that continues on the next amud.

steps.title: Why not reverse the order of the fast day?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא challenges the order just given. Maybe prayer should come first and checking the community's behavior second.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges the order of the fast day it just taught. It suggests flipping it so that prayer comes first and checking the community comes second.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The previous line taught: first half of the day, look into the city's affairs; second half, Torah reading and prayer. The challenger asks what source forces this order. Without a source, the reverse order seems just as reasonable.

keyTerms.meaning: I will reverse it: a challenge that the order or logic could just as well be flipped

phrases.english: I can reverse it!
phrases.notes: This refers to the order just taught: first the community's affairs, then prayer.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the schedule for the fast day taught on the previous amud.
steps.kashyaTarget: The rule that the first half of a fast day is for examining the community and the second half is for prayer.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: No source has been given for this order, so the reverse order should be equally possible.

steps.title: עזרא shows that fixing the community comes before prayer
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא rejects the reversal. In ספר עזרא, the people first gathered over the sin of the exiles, and only at the evening offering did עזרא spread his hands in prayer.
steps.simpleTranslation: Don't think that. It is written: 'Then everyone who trembled at the words of the God of Israel gathered to me because of the sin of the exiles…' And it is written: 'And at the evening offering I rose from my fast and spread out my hands to ה׳.'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the challenge with two פסוקים from עזרא. They show that the gathering about the community's sin happened first, and prayer came later in the day.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The first פסוק describes a gathering to deal with a public sin (intermarriage among the returning exiles). The second פסוק says that only at the time of the evening מנחה did עזרא pray. This sets the order: first examine and fix the community's behavior, then pray.

keyTerms.meaning: It should not enter your mind: an idea is being rejected
The betrayal or sin of the exiles
The evening offering, meaning late afternoon
And I spread out my hands (in prayer)

steps.whatToRemember: On a תענית ציבור, first we examine and fix the community's behavior, and only then we pray. The source is עזרא, chapter 9.

phrases.english: Don't think that,
for it is written: 'And to me gathered'
everyone who trembled at the words of the God of Israel
because of the sin of the exiles, etc.'
phrases.notes: The rest of the פסוק says: 'and I sat stunned until the evening offering.'

phrases.english: And it is written: 'And at the evening offering'
I rose from my fasting
and spread out my hands to ה׳.'

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge of step 1 by bringing a source for the order.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Scriptural source that fixes the order of events
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The order of the fast day could be reversed, with prayer first.
steps.terutzMaskana: The פסוקים in עזרא show that dealing with the community's sin comes first and prayer comes afterward.

steps.title: Bathing on a fast: mourning versus removing pleasure
steps.stepSummary: רב חסדא divides bathing restrictions into two types. If bathing is forbidden because of mourning, both hot and cold water are forbidden. If it is forbidden only to remove pleasure, only hot water is forbidden.
steps.simpleTranslation: רפרם בר פפא said in the name of רב חסדא: Anything forbidden because of mourning, like תשעה באב and a mourner, is forbidden in both hot and cold water. Anything forbidden because of pleasure, like a תענית ציבור, is forbidden in hot water but allowed in cold water.
steps.whatsHappening: A new topic begins. רב חסדא gives a rule explaining when bathing in cold water is allowed and when it is not.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The deciding factor is the reason for the ban. Mourning means we avoid all washing, so cold water is also forbidden. A תענית ציבור only takes away enjoyment, and cold water is not considered enjoyable, so it stays allowed.

keyTerms.meaning: Because of mourning
Because of pleasure or enjoyment
Hot water
Cold water
A public fast declared by the community, for example for rain

steps.whyThisMatters: This sets up the whole rest of this passage. It explains why the laws of washing on תשעה באב are stricter than on other fasts.
steps.confusionAlert: Both kinds of fast forbid bathing. The difference is only how far the ban reaches: mourning bans even cold water, while removing pleasure bans only hot water. Do not think a תענית ציבור allows bathing in general.

phrases.aramaic: אָמַר רַפְרָם בַּר פָּפָּא אָמַר רַב חִסְדָּא:
phrases.english: Rafram bar Pappa said that Rav Chisda said:
Anything that is because of mourning,
such as the Ninth of Av and a mourner,
is forbidden both in hot water and in cold water;
anything that is because of pleasure,
such as a communal fast,
is forbidden in hot water, but permitted in cold water.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַפְרָם בַּר פָּפָּא אָמַר רַב חִסְדָּא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Starts a new topic about the bathing restriction on fasts.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A bathing ban based on mourning covers hot and cold water. A bathing ban based on removing pleasure (תענית ציבור) covers only hot water.

steps.title: A proof from 'they lock the bathhouses'
steps.stepSummary: רב אידי בר אבין brings support from the משנה, which says that on the strict public fasts 'they lock the bathhouses.' This suggests that only hot bathing, the kind done in bathhouses, is forbidden.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב אידי בר אבין said: We also learned this in the משנה: 'And they lock the bathhouses.'
steps.whatsHappening: רב אידי בר אבין tries to support רב חסדא's rule using wording from the משנה about the public fasts.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Bathhouses offered hot water. If the משנה's response to the fast is to lock the bathhouses, it seems only hot bathing is targeted, while cold bathing (in rivers) stays allowed. That matches רב חסדא's rule for a תענית ציבור.

keyTerms.meaning: We too have learned it: a formula bringing support from a משנה or ברייתא
They lock
Bathhouses, places for hot bathing

phrases.english: Rav Idi bar Avin said:
We too have learned this:
'And they lock the bathhouses.'
phrases.notes: Quoted from the משנה about the second series of three public fasts, where bathing is also listed as forbidden.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Brings support from a משנה for רב חסדא's rule.
steps.raayaObject: רב חסדא's rule that on a תענית ציבור hot bathing is forbidden but cold bathing is allowed.
steps.raayaSupportSource: The משנה's phrase 'וְנוֹעֲלִין אֶת הַמֶּרְחֲצָאוֹת', which mentions locking only the hot bathhouses.

steps.title: אביי: you can't dam the rivers
steps.stepSummary: אביי rejects the proof. Even if cold water were forbidden, the משנה could not have said 'they dam the rivers,' since that is impossible. So locking bathhouses proves nothing about cold water.
steps.simpleTranslation: אביי said to him: And if cold water were forbidden, should the משנה have taught 'they dam the rivers'?!
steps.whatsHappening: אביי pushes back on רב אידי's proof. He argues that the משנה mentioned bathhouses only because they are the one thing that can actually be shut down.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The proof assumed that because the משנה only mentions locking bathhouses, cold bathing must be allowed. אביי shows another reason the משנה might mention only bathhouses: there is no practical way to stop people from bathing in rivers. Cold water could still be forbidden; the משנה just had no way to enforce that.

keyTerms.meaning: They dam up or block
Rivers, places for cold bathing
Should it have taught?: introduces a rhetorical push-back

phrases.english: Abaye said to him:
And if cold water were forbidden,
'They dam the rivers'
should it have needed to teach?!
phrases.notes: A rhetorical question: obviously the משנה could not say that, since rivers can't be shut.

steps.triggerLanguage: אֲמַר לֵיהּ אַבָּיֵי: וְאִי בְּצוֹנֵן אָסוּר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Rejects the proof brought in step 4.
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: Rejects only the proof from the משנה. It does not reject רב חסדא's rule itself.
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: Mentioning only bathhouses may simply reflect what can practically be enforced, not that cold water is allowed.

steps.title: רב שישא explains his father's real proof
steps.stepSummary: רב שישא, son of רב אידי, says his father's proof was based on a different point. The משנה already said 'bathing is forbidden,' so the extra phrase 'they lock the bathhouses' must be teaching that only hot bathing is forbidden and cold bathing is allowed.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב שישא, son of רב אידי, said: This is what bothered my father. Since we already learned 'bathing is forbidden,' why do I need 'they lock the bathhouses'? Rather, isn't it clear from here that hot water is forbidden and cold water is allowed?
steps.whatsHappening: רב שישא defends his father against אביי. He explains that the proof comes from an extra phrase in the משנה, not simply from the mention of bathhouses.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The משנה first says 'אָסוּר בִּרְחִיצָה' (bathing is forbidden) and then adds 'נוֹעֲלִין אֶת הַמֶּרְחֲצָאוֹת'. If all bathing were forbidden, the second phrase would add nothing. So it must narrow the first: the ban means hot bathing only. This avoids אביי's objection, which only answered why rivers aren't mentioned, not why the extra phrase is needed.

keyTerms.meaning: This is what was difficult for my father: explaining what was really behind a teacher's statement
Since, after all: introduces an established point
Why do I need it?: points out a phrase that seems extra
Bathing or washing
Rather, isn't it so? Learn from this: draws a conclusion

steps.whatToRemember: The proof for רב חסדא comes from an extra phrase in the משנה. Since 'bathing is forbidden' was already said, 'they lock the bathhouses' must teach that on a תענית ציבור only hot bathing is forbidden, while cold bathing is allowed.

phrases.aramaic: אָמַר רַב שִׁישָׁא בְּרֵיהּ דְּרַב אִידִי:
phrases.english: Rav Sheisha, son of Rav Idi, said:
My father, this is what was difficult for him:
Since we learned: 'bathing is forbidden,'
why do I need 'they lock the bathhouses'?
Rather, isn't it so? Learn from this:
in hot water it is forbidden, in cold water it is permitted.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers אביי's rejection (step 5) by explaining that רב אידי's proof was based on an extra phrase in the משנה.
steps.raayaObject: רב חסדא's rule that on a תענית ציבור hot bathing is forbidden and cold bathing is allowed.
steps.raayaSupportSource: The apparent extra phrase 'נוֹעֲלִין אֶת הַמֶּרְחֲצָאוֹת' following 'אָסוּר בִּרְחִיצָה' in the משנה.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Clarifying the real basis of the original proof
steps.terutzHavaAmina: רב אידי's proof was only that the משנה mentions bathhouses, and אביי answered that rivers simply can't be shut.
steps.terutzMaskana: The proof comes from the extra phrase. Since bathing was already banned, 'locking bathhouses' narrows the ban to hot water, which supports רב חסדא.
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: On a תענית ציבור, bathing in hot water is forbidden and bathing in cold water is allowed, supported by the extra phrase in the משנה.

steps.title: A ברייתא About Immersing on תשעה באב and יום הכפורים
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא suggests that a ברייתא supports רב חסדא. The ברייתא says that anyone who must do a טבילה may immerse as usual on תשעה באב and יום הכפורים.
steps.simpleTranslation: Let us say this supports רב חסדא: Everyone who must immerse may immerse in the normal way, both on תשעה באב and on יום הכפורים.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a ברייתא that might back up רב חסדא. This step only quotes the source. The next step explains why it might prove his point.
steps.deeperAnalysis: תשעה באב is a day of mourning, and on it bathing is forbidden. The ברייתא allows one group, people obligated in טבילה, to go into the water anyway. The גמרא will now ask what kind of water that is, to see what it tells us about everyone else.

keyTerms.meaning: Let us say [this source] supports him
People who are required to do a ritual immersion (e.g., after impurity)
Ritual immersion in a מקוה or natural water
In their usual way

phrases.english: Let us say [the following] supports him:
phrases.notes: 'Him' = רב חסדא, who said a mourning-based bathing ban includes cold water.

phrases.english: All who are obligated in immersions
immerse in their usual manner,
both on the Ninth of Av
and on Yom Kippur.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: After the debate over the משנה of locked bathhouses, the גמרא looks for a new source supporting רב חסדא.
steps.raayaObject: רב חסדא's rule that when bathing is forbidden for mourning, even cold water is forbidden.
steps.raayaSupportSource: A ברייתא permitting חייבי טבילות to immerse on תשעה באב and יום הכפורים.

steps.title: Only Those Who Must Immerse May Use Cold Water
steps.stepSummary: The ברייתא cannot mean hot water, because hot water is drawn water and is invalid for טבילה. So it must mean cold water. That implies only people obligated in טבילה may use cold water, and everyone else may not.
steps.simpleTranslation: What water do they immerse in? If you say hot water, is there such a thing as טבילה in hot water? Hot water is drawn water! So it must be cold water. That means people who must immerse may use it, but anyone else may not.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא explains how the ברייתא proves רב חסדא's point. The ברייתא gives special permission for cold water only to people who need טבילה, so everyone else must be forbidden even cold water.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Hot water must be heated in a vessel, which makes it שאובין (drawn water), and drawn water does not work for טבילה. So the ברייתא must be talking about cold water. If cold water were allowed for everyone, there would be no reason to single out חייבי טבילות. On a mourning day like תשעה באב, then, cold water is forbidden, just as רב חסדא said.

keyTerms.meaning: In what? (asking for the case)
Drawn water, water that passed through a vessel; invalid for טבילה
Cold water
Rather, is it not that... (introduces the forced reading)

steps.confusionAlert: Do not think hot water is a problem because of heat. The problem is that heated water has been in a vessel, so it counts as drawn water, which cannot be used for טבילה.

phrases.english: In what [water]?
If we say in hot water,
is there such a thing as immersion in hot water?
It is drawn water!
phrases.notes: Heated water was put in a vessel, so it is invalid for טבילה.

phrases.english: Rather, is it not in cold water?
And those obligated in immersions — yes [they may],
another person — no [not even in cold].
phrases.notes: This is the inference that supports רב חסדא.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Explains how the ברייתא quoted in step 7 supports רב חסדא.
steps.raayaObject: That cold water is forbidden on a mourning-type day for anyone not obligated in טבילה.
steps.raayaSupportSource: The ברייתא's special permission for חייבי טבילות, which must refer to cold water.

steps.title: The ברייתא Means the Hot Springs of טבריא
steps.stepSummary: רב חנא בר קטינא rejects the proof. The ברייתא is talking about the natural hot springs of טבריא, which are hot but not drawn. So the ברייתא says nothing about cold water.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב חנא בר קטינא said: The ברייתא was needed only for the hot springs of טבריא.
steps.whatsHappening: רב חנא בר קטינא knocks down the proof. He shows the ברייתא could be talking about hot water after all.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The proof depended on the claim that טבילה in hot water is impossible. The hot springs of טבריא are naturally hot and never sat in a vessel, so they are valid for טבילה. The ברייתא can therefore mean that only those who must immerse may use hot water, which tells us nothing about cold water.

keyTerms.meaning: It was needed only for... (narrows the case)
The natural hot springs of Tiberias

phrases.english: Rav Ḥana bar Ketina said:
It was needed only for the hot springs of Tiberias.
phrases.notes: Natural hot water is not 'drawn', so טבילה in it is valid.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Rejects the inference of step 8 by offering another case for the ברייתא.
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: Rejects the claim that the ברייתא must be referring to cold water.
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: The proof assumed hot-water טבילה is impossible, but natural hot springs are valid.

steps.title: Why Lose the Immersion If Cold Water Is Allowed?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא challenges רב חנא בר קטינא from the סיפא. רבי חנינא סגן הכהנים says it is worth losing a טבילה once a year for the Temple. If cold water were permitted, why lose the טבילה at all?
steps.simpleTranslation: If so, look at the end of the ברייתא: רבי חנינא סגן הכהנים said, 'The House of our God deserves that we give up a טבילה over it once a year.' But if you say cold water is permitted, let the person just bathe in cold water!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא attacks רב חנא בר קטינא's reading. It uses the very next line of the same ברייתא.
steps.deeperAnalysis: According to רב חנא בר קטינא, the ban covers only hot water, so cold water stays permitted. But רבי חנינא speaks of 'losing' a טבילה on תשעה באב. If cold water were allowed, nobody would lose anything, because he could simply immerse in cold water. The wording 'losing' suggests that cold water is also forbidden.

keyTerms.meaning: If so (introduces a challenge based on the last answer)
Say [look at] the latter clause
Deputy High Priest
To lose / give up

phrases.english: If so, say the latter clause:
Rabbi Ḥanina, the deputy High Priest, said:
The House of our God is worthy
of losing an immersion on its account
once a year.
phrases.notes: That is, on תשעה באב, the day of mourning for the Temple.

phrases.english: And if you say that in cold water it is permitted —
let him bathe in cold water!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the דחיה of step 9 using the סיפא of the same ברייתא.
steps.kashyaTarget: רב חנא בר קטינא's reading that only hot water is restricted, leaving cold water permitted.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: If cold water were allowed, no one would ever have to 'lose' a טבילה. So the סיפא implies that cold water is forbidden too.

steps.title: A Place Without Cold Water
steps.stepSummary: רב פפא answers that רבי חנינא is talking about a place where no cold water is available. There the only option is the hot springs, which are forbidden, so the טבילה really is lost.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב פפא said: It is talking about a place where cold water is not available.
steps.whatsHappening: רב פפא defends רב חנא בר קטינא's reading against the challenge from the סיפא.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Cold water may be permitted in principle, but in some places there is none, only hot springs. Since hot bathing is forbidden on the fast day, a person there must put off his טבילה until the next day. That is what 'losing' the טבילה means, so the proof for רב חסדא remains undone.

keyTerms.meaning: In a place
Is not found / not available

phrases.english: Rav Pappa said:
[It refers] to a place where cold water is not available.

steps.terutzResolutionType: Limiting the case: placing the סיפא in a specific situation.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Speaking of 'losing' a טבילה must mean that cold water is forbidden.
steps.terutzMaskana: The loss happens only where cold water is unavailable. So the ברייתא does not prove רב חסדא's view.
steps.whatToRemember: The attempt to prove רב חסדא from the ברייתא of חייבי טבילות fails. The ברייתא can refer to the hot springs of טבריא, and the 'lost' טבילה refers to a place without cold water.

steps.title: Limits on Work, Shoes, and Bathing on Fast Days
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא opens a new source with תא שמע. A ברייתא limits the fast-day bans: work only by day, shoes only in the city, and bathing only of the whole body (face, hands and feet are allowed). It adds that the same is true for a מנודה and an אבל.
steps.simpleTranslation: Come and hear: When they said work is forbidden, they meant only by day, but at night it is permitted. When they said wearing shoes is forbidden, they meant only in the city, but on the road it is permitted. How so? When he goes out on the road he puts shoes on, and when he enters the city he takes them off. When they said bathing is forbidden, they meant only the whole body, but his face, hands and feet are permitted. You find the same with a מנודה and with an אבל.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a new ברייתא to test רב חסדא's rule. This step only quotes the source. Its exact use for or against רב חסדא is worked out right after this.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The ברייתא lists limits on three fast-day bans and then says the same limits apply to a מנודה and an אבל. That comparison matters: it links the fast-day bathing ban to the mourner's bathing ban. רב חסדא had separated these two types of bans, so this link will be the point the גמרא tests.

keyTerms.meaning: Come and hear (introduces a source to prove or challenge)
Work
Wearing shoes
Bathing / washing
A person placed under a formal ban (excommunication)
A mourner

steps.whyThisMatters: This ברייתא sets real limits on fast-day bans: work is forbidden only by day, shoes only in town, and bathing only of the whole body. It also ties these rules to the rules of a mourner.

phrases.english: Come and hear:
When they said 'one is forbidden to work' —
they said it only about the daytime,
but at night — it is permitted.
And when they said 'one is forbidden to wear shoes' —
they said it only about the city,
but on the road — it is permitted.
How so?
When he goes out on the road — he puts on shoes,
when he enters the city — he takes them off.
And when they said 'one is forbidden to bathe' —
they said it only about his whole body,
but his face, hands and feet — it is permitted,
and likewise you find with one who is banned and with a mourner.
phrases.notes: This line links the fast-day rules to the mourner's rules, which is the key point for רב חסדא.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: After the first proof was deflected (steps 7–11), the גמרא brings a new ברייתא to test רב חסדא's distinction.
steps.raayaObject: רב חסדא's distinction between mourning-based and pleasure-based bathing bans.
steps.raayaSupportSource: A ברייתא that limits the fast-day bans and compares them to a מנודה and an אבל.

steps.title: The fast-day ברייתא must be talking about cold water
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא finishes the proof from the ברייתא in Step 12. The 'same for a מנודה and an אבל' line covers all the rules, including washing. Since an אבל may not touch hot water at all, the ברייתא must mean cold water. So washing the whole body even in cold water is forbidden.
steps.simpleTranslation: Doesn't the line 'the same is true for a מנודה and an אבל' apply to all the rules, including washing? Now, what kind of washing are we talking about? If you say hot water: are face, hands and feet really allowed for an אבל? But רב ששת said that an אבל may not even put his finger into hot water! So it must be talking about cold water.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא is finishing the proof it opened in Step 12. It shows that the ברייתא must be talking about cold water.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The ברייתא allowed washing face, hands and feet, and said the same rules apply to an אבל. רב ששת forbids an אבל to put even one finger in hot water. So the allowed partial washing cannot be in hot water; it must be cold water. That means washing the whole body in cold water is forbidden, on a fast day and for an אבל.

keyTerms.meaning: On all of them: the line applies to every rule listed
We are dealing with (what case is this?)
Hot water
Cold water
A mourner
To stick out his finger (into the water)

steps.confusionAlert: The proof only works if the 'same for מנודה and אבל' line covers the washing rule too. That is exactly the point the next step attacks.

phrases.english: Is it not that it refers to all of them?
phrases.notes: The line about מנודה and אבל covers every rule, including washing.

phrases.english: And with what are we dealing?
If you say with hot water:
are his face, his hands and his feet permitted?
But didn't Rav Sheshet say:
a mourner is forbidden to put his finger into hot water!
Rather, is it not with cold water!
phrases.notes: So bathing the whole body even in cold water would be forbidden.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Draws out the conclusion of the ברייתא quoted in Step 12.
steps.raayaObject: That washing the whole body even in cold water is forbidden on a fast day and for an אבל.
steps.raayaSupportSource: The fast-day ברייתא from Step 12, combined with רב ששת's ruling about hot water for an אבל.

steps.title: The ברייתא really means hot water
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא rejects the proof. The ברייתא does mean hot water. The line 'the same for a מנודה and an אבל' refers only to the other rules (work and shoes), not to washing.
steps.simpleTranslation: No. Really, the ברייתא is talking about hot water. And what bothered you, the line 'the same is true for a מנודה and an אבל'? That line refers to the other rules, not to washing.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא pushes off the proof from Step 13. It reads the ברייתא as talking about hot water.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The whole proof depended on the מנודה and אבל line covering washing. Now the גמרא says that line covers only work and shoes. So the washing rule is only about a fast day and only about hot water, and cold water on a fast day stays permitted.

keyTerms.meaning: Really, actually (sticking with the first reading)
A person under a ban (נידוי)
It refers to the rest (of the rules)

phrases.english: No, actually it is with hot water.
And what was difficult for you,
'and similarly you find with one under a ban and with a mourner':
it refers to the rest.
phrases.notes: Meaning work and shoes, not washing.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Rejects the inference drawn in Step 13.
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: Full rejection of the proof from the fast-day ברייתא.
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: The proof assumed the מנודה and אבל line covers washing. It may cover only the other rules.

steps.title: A story: a mourner who bathed in cold water
steps.stepSummary: A new proof is brought. When the sons of רבי יוסי בן רבי חנינא died, he bathed in cold water all seven days of mourning. This suggests that an אבל may bathe in cold water.
steps.simpleTranslation: Come and hear: רבי אבא הכהן said in the name of רבי יוסי הכהן: It once happened that the sons of רבי יוסי בן רבי חנינא died, and he bathed in cold water all seven days!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a new source, a story about a great sage. It suggests that an אבל may bathe in cold water.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This time the proof points the other way from Step 13: cold-water bathing seems permitted for an אבל. A sage actually did it for the full שבעה. If an אבל may do it, then surely it is allowed on a fast day.

keyTerms.meaning: Come and hear (a new source is introduced)
An incident, a story that actually happened
The seven days of mourning

phrases.aramaic: תָּא שְׁמַע, דְּאָמַר רַבִּי אַבָּא הַכֹּהֵן
phrases.english: Come and hear, as Rabbi Abba the priest said
in the name of Rabbi Yosei the priest:
An incident where the sons died

phrases.aramaic: שֶׁל רַבִּי יוֹסֵי בֶּן רַבִּי חֲנִינָא,
phrases.english: of Rabbi Yosei son of Rabbi Chanina,
and he bathed in cold water all seven days!

steps.triggerLanguage: תָּא שְׁמַע, דְּאָמַר רַבִּי אַבָּא הַכֹּהֵן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: After the first proof was rejected, a new source is brought on the same question.
steps.raayaObject: That an אבל, and so also someone on a fast day, may bathe in cold water.
steps.raayaSupportSource: The story of רבי יוסי בן רבי חנינא, told by רבי אבא הכהן in the name of רבי יוסי הכהן.

steps.title: His case was special: mournings one after another
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא rejects the proof. רבי יוסי's mournings came one right after another, and such a mourner gets special leniencies. A ברייתא says he may trim heavy hair with a razor and wash his clothes in water.
steps.simpleTranslation: There, it was a case where his mournings pressed on him one after another. As a ברייתא teaches: If one's mournings came one after another and his hair became heavy, he may lighten it with a razor and wash his clothing in water.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא pushes off the proof from the story. It says the story was an unusual case.
steps.deeperAnalysis: His sons died one after another, so his mourning periods stacked up with no break. A ברייתא gives such a mourner relief that a normal אבל does not get: cutting hair and washing clothes. His cold-water bathing fits this special leniency, so it teaches nothing about a normal אבל or a fast day.

keyTerms.meaning: His mournings pressed on him, coming one right after another
As it is taught in a ברייתא
He lightens (his hair) with a razor
His clothing

steps.whyThisMatters: It shows that a lenient story about an אבל cannot be used as a general rule if the case had special circumstances.

phrases.english: There it was when his mournings came one after another,

phrases.aramaic: דְּתַנְיָא: תְּכָפוּהוּ אֲבָלָיו זֶה אַחַר זֶה,
phrases.english: as it is taught: if his mournings came one after another,
and his hair became heavy, he may lighten it with a razor,
and he may wash his clothing in water.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Rejects the proof from the story in Step 15.
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: Full rejection: the story proves nothing about a normal אבל.
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: The story was an exceptional case of stacked mournings, which has its own leniencies.

steps.title: Razor but not scissors; water but not soap or sand
steps.stepSummary: רב חסדא limits the leniency of the ברייתא. The hair may be cut with a razor but not with scissors. The clothes may be washed in plain water but not with natron (soap) or sand.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב חסדא said: With a razor, but not with scissors. In water, but not with natron and not with sand.
steps.whatsHappening: רב חסדא explains the limits of the ברייתא just quoted about a mourner whose mournings came one after another.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Even this special mourner does not get full freedom. He may trim his hair only with a razor, which is not the normal way, not with scissors. He may wash his clothes only lightly in water, without soap or sand that would clean them thoroughly.

keyTerms.meaning: Scissors
Natron, a soap-like cleaning mineral
Sand (used for scrubbing)

steps.whatToRemember: Both proofs about cold-water bathing were pushed off. The fast-day ברייתא may mean hot water, and the story of רבי יוסי בן רבי חנינא was a special case of stacked mournings. Even that special mourner gets only limited relief: a razor and plain water.

phrases.english: Rav Chisda said:
With a razor, but not with scissors;
in water, but not with natron and not with sand.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Explains and limits the ברייתא quoted in Step 16.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A mourner whose mournings came one after another may cut his hair only with a razor, not scissors. He may wash clothes only in water, not with natron or sand.

steps.title: רבא permits a mourner to bathe in cold water
steps.stepSummary: רבא rules that an אבל may bathe in cold water for all seven days of mourning. He compares it to meat and wine, which an אבל is allowed to have.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבא said: An אבל is allowed to wash in cold water all seven days, just like he is allowed to have meat and wine.
steps.whatsHappening: After the earlier proofs were pushed away, רבא now gives a direct ruling: an אבל may bathe in cold water during שבעה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבא disagrees with רב חסדא, who forbade an אבל to bathe even in cold water. He argues by comparison: meat and wine give a person pleasure, yet an אבל may still have them, so a cold-water bath is also allowed even though it feels good. This ruling does not settle the matter, because the גמרא immediately challenges it.

keyTerms.meaning: A mourner (during the first seven days after a close relative's death)
Cold water
All seven days of mourning
Just like (a formula for comparing one case to another)
Meat and wine

steps.whyThisMatters: This is the first clear ruling in the sugya that allows cold-water bathing for an אבל. The next step announces a challenge to it, and that challenge continues on the next amud.

phrases.english: Rava said:
phrases.notes: Attribution line. It introduces רבא's ruling.

phrases.english: A mourner is permitted to bathe in cold water
all seven days,
just as it is with meat and wine.
phrases.notes: An אבל may eat meat and drink wine even though they give pleasure. So a pleasant cold bath is also allowed.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רָבָא: אָבֵל מוּתָּר לִרְחוֹץ בְּצוֹנֵן כׇּל שִׁבְעָה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: After the challenge from רבי יוסי בן רבי חנינא's story was answered, רבא states the lenient view directly, against רב חסדא, supported by a comparison.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: An אבל may bathe in cold water throughout the seven days, just as he may eat meat and drink wine.

steps.title: The גמרא announces a challenge to רבא
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא says 'מיתיבי', which means it is about to bring a source that seems to contradict רבא's ruling.
steps.simpleTranslation: They challenged him from a source:
steps.whatsHappening: This is a setup line. The גמרא is getting ready to quote a source that will challenge רבא's ruling that an אבל may bathe in cold water.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The word מיתיבי always introduces an objection from a תנאי source, such as a משנה or ברייתא. The actual text of the objection comes next. For now, the learner should expect a source that seems to forbid an אבל from bathing, even in cold water.

keyTerms.meaning: 'They raised an objection.' It introduces a challenge from a משנה or ברייתא.

steps.confusionAlert: The challenge itself is not here yet. This line only announces it, so don't look for the objection's content in this step.

phrases.english: They raised an objection:
phrases.notes: Introduces a תנאי source that will challenge רבא on the next amud.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Opens an objection against רבא's ruling in Step 18.
steps.kashyaTarget: רבא's ruling that an אבל may bathe in cold water all seven days.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: A תנאי source (quoted at the start of the next amud) will appear to contradict רבא's leniency.
